- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/12/10 (Sun) 21:02
- [USER] User expressed interest in Wicca and its principles and practices.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wicca principles include worship of nature, the Goddess and the God, rituals and spellwork, ethics (Wiccan Rede), and coven-based practice.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wicca emphasizes the worship of the Goddess, dualism between feminine and masculine divine, coven-based practice, and a specific ethical code (Wiccan Rede) compared to other neo-pagan religions.
- [USER] User found the information about Wicca interesting and inquired about specific holidays or seasonal events celebrated by Wiccans.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wiccans celebrate eight major seasonal festivals known as Sabbats, divided into Greater Sabbats and Lesser Sabbats.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Greater Sabbats include: 
  1. Samhain (October 31st)
  2. Yule (Winter Solstice, around December 21st)
  3. Imbolc (February 2nd)
  4. Ostara (Spring Equinox, around March 20th)
  5. Beltane (May 1st)
  6. Litha (Summer Solstice, around June 21st)
  7. Lammas/Lughnasadh (August 1st)
  8. Mabon (Autumn Equinox, around September 21st)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Lesser Sabbats include the Four Quarter Days and Cross-Quarter Days, with specific dates mentioned.
- [USER] User expressed interest in learning about special practices during Wiccan celebrations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wiccans engage in rituals during Sabbats, including creating a sacred space, honoring deities, and connecting with nature.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Specific customs for Sabbats include building an altar on Samhain, lighting a Yule log on Yule, and holding ceremonial feasts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wiccans may perform spellwork, meditations, and divination during celebrations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Coven-based Wiccans celebrate Sabbats in groups led by a High Priestess or High Priest, while solitary practitioners perform personal rituals.
